title: A screen lock makes the notary profile unreadable, so a cut's macOS stage fails at its notary submit when the Mac locks after pre-flight
body:
Filed by dc for devbin 0.1.34, on vc's word, from Gtools' 0.10.0 cut of 2026-11-25. Line numbers are at v0.1.33.

## What happens

Gtools' 0.10.0 cut ran on its vendored devbin 0.1.33. It passed pre-flight, made its release commit and pushed its candidate. Its macOS stage then failed at the notary submit with "Error: No Keychain password item found for profile: devbin" (Gtools tmp/release/20261125-1728.MACOS.out:46). The cut stopped at the legs step, deleted its candidate and tagged nothing.

The pre-flight's `macos doctor` (issue 0366, lib/cmd/release:3149-3165) had passed about 70 seconds before. Its notarytool history query read the same profile at 17:28:54Z, and both of its requests to Apple returned 200.

## Why

The profile on rhadamanth is a data-protection keychain item. secd holds it in class 6, and secd reads such an item only while the session is unlocked. At 17:29:17Z the display dimmed, and loginwindow locked the screen and the keybag at once ("kLWLockFromDisplayDim", "normal lock", delay 0). At 17:30:03Z secd refused the stage's read with -25308 errSecInteractionNotAllowed: "ks_crypt: e00002e2 failed to 'od' item (class 6, bag: -3) Access to item attempted while keychain is locked." notarytool reports this refusal as "No Keychain password item found".

The Developer ID key is in the login keychain file, and a screen lock does not lock that file. So the stage signed the app after the lock. A doctor run at 17:34:18Z, with the screen still locked, passed its test-sign and failed only its notary row.

So the pre-flight's check is correct at its own moment, and nothing keeps it true after. A cut with a macOS stage fails when the Mac locks between the pre-flight and the end of the notary submit. That happens when a cut runs while nobody uses the Mac, once the display dims. devbin passes notarytool `--keychain-profile` alone (lib/cmd/macos:383, 389, 1378 and 1396), so notarytool picks the keychain, and devbin's store-creds names none either.

Nothing deleted the profile, and the pre-flight keeps doctor's exit code. `gate_exec` returns its command's status, and the launcher runs lib/cmd/macos with exec (run_command, exec_handler).

## Evidence

All times are UTC. They come from rhadamanth's unified log, converted from its +04 local time, and from ioreg.

- 17:28:54Z, notarytool, the pre-flight doctor's history query: the keychain read passed, and both requests returned 200.
- 17:29:17Z, loginwindow: the screen and the keybag locked on display dim. ioreg's CGSSessionScreenLockedTime gives the same second.
- 17:29:44Z: the macOS stage started, and it signed the app.
- 17:30:03Z, secd: it refused the read of the profile, -25308, class 6.
- 17:30:09Z: the stage ended with exit 1.
- 17:34:18Z: a doctor run, with the screen still locked. The test-sign passed, and the notary profile read NOT USABLE.

Cross-check: Intent's 5 macOS stages since 22 Nov were all Accepted. Each ran with the session unlocked from its start to its end, by loginwindow's lock and unlock events. Utilz's stages of 10 Nov failed, passed, failed and passed. The unified log does not go back to 10 Nov, so those cannot be checked.

## Fix

1. Every notarytool call devbin makes passes `--keychain` with the login keychain file, `~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db`, beside `--keychain-profile`. That is store-credentials in store-creds, and submit, log and history. One function in lib/cmd/macos makes the two options, and each call uses it. notarytool's own option text says that `--keychain` reads and stores in the file it names, and that it cannot be used with `--sync`.
2. doctor reads the profile through the same function, so the pre-flight checks what the stage reads.
3. The submit's refusal names notarytool's reason. It stops telling the person to store a profile that can exist.

hv then stores the profile once more with `bin/devbin macos store-creds` on each Mac that cuts. The data-protection copy can stay, since with `--keychain` notarytool reads only the file it names.

Until 0.1.34 ships, a cut with a macOS stage needs hv at the Mac, with the session unlocked from the pre-flight to the end of the notary submit. A pre-flight that runs while the screen is locked refuses at doctor, before anything is stamped.

## Proof

- An arm in macos.bats: the notarytool stub records its arguments, and every call carries `--keychain` with the login keychain file. The arm goes red on 0.1.33's lib/cmd/macos.
- On rhadamanth, after store-creds: lock the screen (`pmset displaysleepnow`), then run `bin/devbin macos doctor`. Its notary row reads PRESENT while the screen is locked.

## Resolution

Fixed in the devbin 0.1.34 batch. The fix landed at 2743dbcd58d22697919f908cbfcfe8331cca3424 on main, by fast-forward from 81a93d76.

Fix: every notarytool call devbin makes names the login keychain file, ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db, with --keychain, beside --keychain-profile. One function in lib/cmd/macos, notary_auth, gives the options to submit, log and doctor's history query, and store-creds gives the same file to store-credentials. doctor therefore reads the profile as the submit reads it. A submit that gets no submission id names the keychain file and notarytool's Error: line. It tells the person to run doctor, and to run store-creds only if doctor reads the profile NOT USABLE.

Proof on the Desk, slot 01M8B5V7STJ1RFHJCY33QEHG76, 2026-11-26 05:39Z to 05:44Z: the new macos.bats arm was red at base 81a93d76, because no notarytool call named the login keychain file, and green at the tip. macos.bats whole at the tip read 67 of 67 ok.

Live proof on rhadamanth, 2026-11-26, from the bank, with hv at the Mac. Times are UTC, from the results file and the unified log:
- 05:46:10Z to 05:46:12Z: store-creds stored the profile, and securityd committed login.keychain-db.
- 05:46:28Z: the screen and the keybag locked on display dim ("normal lock"). The screen stayed locked until 05:46:58Z.
- 05:46:38Z to 05:46:54Z: secd refused class 6 reads as locked (-25308), so the data-protection keychain was locked.
- 05:46:51Z: the fix's doctor read the profile PRESENT, and its test-sign signed and verified.
- 05:46:53Z: notarytool history with --keychain and --keychain-profile passed. Like doctor's read, it opened the login file and made no data-protection read.
- 05:46:54Z: notarytool history with --keychain-profile alone (the 0.1.33 call) tried the data-protection keychain first, and secd refused it with -25308. notarytool then read the profile from the login file, which is on the search list, and the read passed.

The script's first verdict read NOT DECIDED, because it took the 0.1.33 call as its control. Once the login file holds the profile, that call passes while locked, by notarytool's fallback to the file. The script now takes its control from the unified log: secd must refuse a notarytool read with -25308 inside the lock window. On this run that count is 1, so the verdict is PROVED.

The old data-protection copy of the profile is still there. secd failed to decrypt a matching class 6 item for the 0.1.33 call. The fix never reads it. Leave it in place: a caller that names no keychain reads it while the Mac is unlocked, and reads the login file's copy while the Mac is locked.

After 0.1.34 ships, run bin/devbin macos store-creds once on each Mac that cuts. rhadamanth's login keychain file holds the profile from 2026-11-26 05:46Z.
